answer.rationale: memory_c2 shows the low-cost vendor previously delivered accurate invoicing and quick onboarding at sharp unit cost reduction, which directly supports switching primary supply to the vendor whose quote already meets the 18% mandate. The incumbent has refused to reopen price, so renewing would not satisfy finance. Switching primary also avoids the delivery risk of running single-source with a contract that does not auto-renew. The one accepted risk: dropping the incumbent fully removes a known-stable supplier, so delivery risk rises slightly versus renewal — but the low-cost vendor's prior track record on accuracy and onboarding mitigates that, and TCO dominates given the mandate. Add_second_source and negotiate_terms both consume the single-decision slot without meeting the 18% cut on their own; defer_decision would push the decision past the 14-day expiry and create a service gap.
